Reason: The chest X-ray shows a central venous catheter entering from the left side and coursing horizontally across the midline into the left brachiocephalic vein rather than descending vertically into the superior vena cava. This malposition is associated with risks of extravasation and mediastinal complications, especially during chemotherapy infusion.
